$comment: Hard marginal gzip KiB ceilings for splitting-aware production ESM. Each route adds one anchored component to the representative shell in $baseline. Initial bytes include only the entry and transitively static chunks; dynamic chunks remain covered by total-cost budgets. Ceilings retain at most 4% drift. Locale-picker's optional text filter adds localized matching, editable input and IME handling, keyboard focus/navigation, and an empty state. Its reviewed 24,921-byte initial marginal measurement retains a 2% allowance at 25,419 bytes; the shell, optional-peer exclusions and other ceilings are unchanged. Semantic popover trigger ownership measures 16,828 initial marginal gzip bytes versus 16,403 for published 25.5.0 under the same toolchain and dependencies. Its 17,038-byte ceiling preserves the previous 210-byte allowance; the 51,948-byte shell and every other route ceiling are unchanged. Changed initial routes use their exact measured marginal gzip sizes with failing ceilings rounded up to 64-byte boundaries; the shared shell and passing ceilings remain unchanged. Callable loader routes retain their named exports during measurement: CDN 13,059 bytes, autoloader 12,878, locale loader 1,469, scoped-registry loader 11,201. These initial-route ceilings and the remaining native form, editing, disclosure and lifecycle costs use the next 64-byte boundary. Passing marginal ceilings, shell imports and peer exclusions remain unchanged. The final callable CDN and scoped-registry routes advance only their failing ceilings to the next 64-byte boundary; all passing initial and marginal ceilings remain unchanged.
